name: What is the difference between a main sewer cleanout and a branch cleanout?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a main sewer cleanout and a branch cleanout?

acceptedAnswer.text: A main sewer cleanout provides direct access to the primary sewer line that carries all wastewater from your home to the municipal sewer system or septic tank. A branch cleanout, on the other hand, accesses a smaller branch line serving a specific area or fixture, like a bathroom or kitchen. Understanding this distinction is important because while a main cleanout addresses widespread issues, a branch cleanout is useful for isolated clogs. Our technicians can help identify which type of access point is most beneficial for your property's plumbing needs.
acceptedAnswer.description: A main sewer cleanout accesses the primary sewer line, while a branch cleanout accesses a smaller line serving specific fixtures; both serve different diagnostic and clearing needs.
